sections.content:
12,830 people

were counted on the census as "dancers and choreographers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Dancers and choreographers devise, direct, rehearse and perform classical and contemporary dance routines.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "dancers and choreographers" there were more women than men (84% compared with 16%).

This means "dancers and choreographers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "culture, media and sports occupations".

Men made up 15.9% and women made up 84.1% of "dancers and choreographers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "dancers and choreographers" included:

  • health associate professionals (other)
  • child and early years officers
  • pharmaceutical technicians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "dancers and choreographers", 18.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "dancers and choreographers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "dancers and choreographers" included:

  • quantity surveyors
  • actors, entertainers and presenters
  • business and related research professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "dancers and choreographers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "dancers and choreographers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "dancers and choreographers", 7.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (77.3% compared with 22.7%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (80.8%) than an employee (19.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
